title: Wringer certificate
description: One `certificate.json`, written by `wring deliver` into the delivery beside `mr.md`. **A NEW FILE, and no published schema changes for it** — the frozen-schema law's whole point is that a sibling is always allowed and an amendment never is. This is the portable form of what a run already recorded: every requirement the approved spec declares, what the record can honestly say about each, and — for the ones a check proves — where that check is on record failing. **It re-assesses nothing.** Every requirement fact is copied out of the run's `acceptance.json`; a second assessor would be a second opinion about one run, and the two would drift. **The face grows and this record does not.** It carries exactly the facts this version earns, and there are deliberately no empty keys held open for facts a later version might add: a key present and null is a claim that the question was asked and came back empty, which is the absence-as-verdict failure this project exists to refuse. A later fact rides its own sibling record and the face renders it where it finds it. What this document is NOT is in `limits`, travelling on the document rather than in a spec nobody opened, and it is the acceptance record's own ceiling PLUS this one's — a shorter list on the more portable artifact would be the ceiling quietly falling as the claim travels further.

written_at.description: ISO-8601, when `wring deliver` wrote this. The machine's clock, recorded and not checked.

change.description: What is being handed over. Enough for a reader to know which change this is about, and no more: there is no author, no committer and no agent name anywhere in this record, because the offline check must not be able to read one. A verification whose answer moves when the author changes is a verification of the author.

title.description: The approved spec's title, or the task, or the run. Never invented — it is taken from something a person wrote.

commit.description: The commit the gates were verified against, or null when the tree could not be read. Checked by `wring audit` against the clone in front of the reader.

run.description: The run whose record this document renders.

bundle.description: Repo-relative, like every other cross-bundle reference in this program — never absolute, because an artifact whose whole purpose is that a stranger can read it must not carry somebody's home directory.

spec.description: The document the work was authorised by. `sha256` is over `wringer.spec.yaml`'s bytes, and `wring audit` re-hashes the clone's copy: a mismatch says the spec moved after the run, which is a fact the reader needs and is not by itself a forgery.

acceptance.description: Which acceptance version this was rendered from, and its counts verbatim. The counts are carried rather than recomputed so that `wring audit` can check the summary against the rows — the cheapest forgery is an edited number over honest rows.

requirements.description: Every requirement the approved spec declares, in the order it declares them. **Sorted by nothing.** Ranking these would be this document deciding which debts matter, which is the reader's call — the same refusal `acceptance.json` makes, for the same reason.

id.description: The criterion id from `wringer.spec.yaml`, never slugged or normalised: it is the join key `wring audit` uses against the clone's spec, and a normalised join is a silent mis-bind.

state.description: The acceptance record's own state word, carried unchanged. It is here for the machine; nothing renders it to a reader.

says.description: The plain-English label a reader sees, IN the record. The reviewer's first gap was that `unevidenced` is not a word they use — so the words a person reads travel with the row rather than being re-derived by every surface that renders it. A `(state, cause)` pair the renderer has no wording for produces an explicit refusal to translate, never the nearest phrase.

means.description: The same fact as a sentence: what this state means for the person deciding whether to merge.

check.description: The gate whose `proves:` names this requirement, or null when nothing binds it. Null is a DEBT, not an error.

receipt.description: Where the record shows this check failing, copied from the acceptance row, or null. This is what `wring audit` re-checks per receipt — and where the run it names did not travel with the document, the audit says so in those words rather than counting it either way.

reason.description: The engine's own prose for this state, carried verbatim. It holds the remedy, and this document does not regenerate it from the label above.

judgement.description: A person's answer to a requirement only a person can settle, copied from the acceptance row, or null. It carries the verdict, the name, the date and — the reason this key is here at all — the NOTE. A note reading `your words here5` reached a delivered branch as the stated reason a requirement passed, and was caught only by somebody opening the YAML, because no surface in the program showed a judgement note to anybody.

limits.description: What this document does NOT say. The acceptance record's list, plus this document's own — never fewer.
